implementation_notes: The BCL ships the bounded pull: BlockingCollection<T>.TryTake(item, timeout, cancellationToken) returns false when the interval expires (the idle tick) and CompleteAdding()/IsCompleted is the real end-of-stream signal, while the acknowledgement is whatever the producer-consumer contract requires (task completion, a database commit, a broker's complete/abandon call). System.Threading.Channels provides the async form with the same semantics (ChannelReader<T>.ReadAsync/WaitToReadAsync plus a CancellationToken for shutdown), and broker SDKs mirror the shape with receive-with-max-wait overloads, so a hand-written loop is only needed for an in-process queue the framework does not already wrap.
pitfalls: TryTake returning false means 'nothing within the interval', not 'channel closed'; a consumer that treats it as end-of-stream exits on the first quiet period, so IsCompleted/CompleteAdding must be the loop condition.
Omitting the CancellationToken makes shutdown block behind a full-blocking take; the token has to be threaded through every TryTake/ReadAsync and through the handler's awaits.
